name: Hazael king of Syria
charge: Smothering his master with a wet cloth to take the throne, and doing to Israel the evil Elisha wept over
summary: When Ben-hadad lay sick and sent Hazael with forty camel loads of gifts to ask Elisha whether he would recover, the prophet fixed his eyes on him and wept, because he saw the evil Hazael would do to Israel: burning their strongholds, killing their young men, dashing their children and ripping open pregnant women (2 Kings 8:7-12). Hazael went back, smothered his master with a wet cloth, and took the throne, and the Lord used him to cut Israel short (2 Kings 8:15; 2 Kings 10:32). By Amos the Lord said He would send fire on the house of Hazael and carry Syria captive to Kir (Amos 1:3-5).
offenseFull: At Horeb the Lord told Elijah to anoint Hazael king over Syria, Jehu over Israel, and Elisha as prophet, and whoever escaped the sword of Hazael, Jehu would kill (1 Kings 19:15-17). The Most High had things set up, and Syria would come against the northern kingdom. When Elisha came to Damascus, Ben-hadad was sick and sent Hazael with a present of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ load, to ask whether he would recover (2 Kings 8:7-9). The word of a prophet was precious in those days. The Syrians had their own gods, yet their king sent to the God of Israel; they knew there was only one true and living God, and that did not stop them fighting against us.

Elisha told him to tell the king he could recover, though the Lord had shown him that he would surely die; then he fixed his gaze on Hazael until the man was ashamed, and wept (2 Kings 8:10-11). Asked why, he said he knew the evil Hazael would do to the children of Israel: set their strongholds on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their children, and rip open their women with child (2 Kings 8:12). Hazael had done none of it yet. The prophet saw years ahead that he would be an instrument of terror; prophecy has no time clock, and leadership can discern a spirit at work in a man that the man cannot see in himself. Hazael asked whether he was a dog, to do such a thing, and Elisha answered that the Lord had shown him Hazael would be king over Syria (2 Kings 8:13). Hazael went back, told his master he would recover,

and the next day took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over the king’s face until he died, and reigned in his place (2 Kings 8:14-15). The teaching names the murdered king Ben-hadad the second.
judgmentFull: What Elisha wept over came. Jehu destroyed Baal but kept Jeroboam’s calves and did not walk in the law with all his heart, and in those days the Lord began to cut Israel short: Hazael struck them in all the land east of the Jordan, Gilead, Gad, Reuben and Manasseh, from Aroer by the Arnon to Bashan (2 Kings 10:31-33). When we sin, the Lord brings an adversary, other nations, to correct us. Hazael took Gath and set his face against Jerusalem, and Jehoash of Judah bought him off with the hallowed things of the house of the Lord (2 Kings 12:17-18). The Lord’s anger gave Israel into the hand of Hazael and his son all the days of Jehoahaz, yet He was gracious to them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (2 Kings 13:3, 22-23). The teacher sets the ripping open of pregnant women beside what was done to our people in American slavery; no nation has suffered as Israel has under the curses of the law (Daniel 9:11-12).

Even though the Lord used him, He would judge him. Through Amos the Lord said that for three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, He would not turn back its punishment, because they had threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron; He would send fire into the house of Hazael to devour the palaces of Ben-hadad, break the bar of Damascus, and send the people of Syria captive to Kir (Amos 1:3-5). Threshing Gilead means they thrashed it and took the whole east side of the Jordan. Prophecy is fulfilled in layers. Hazael died and his son Ben-hadad reigned, and Jehoash of Israel beat him three times and took back the cities; then Jeroboam the second recovered Damascus and Hamath, which the teachers read as the fire on Hazael’s house (2 Kings 13:24-25; 2 Kings 14:28). The captivity came when Tiglath-pileser took Damascus, carried its people to Kir and killed Rezin (2 Kings 16:9). One teacher adds a further layer still to come on the nations at the end.

text.text: And Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben–hadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.
And the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and go, meet the man of God, and enquire of the Lord by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?

So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Ben–hadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the Lord hath shewed me that he shall surely die.
And he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept.

And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.
And it came to pass on the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
In those days the Lord began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel;
Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron:
But I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which shall devour the palaces of Ben–hadad.

I will break also the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the plain of Aven, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of Eden: and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir, saith the Lord.
And the Lord said unto him, Go, return on thy way to the wilderness of Damascus: and when thou comest, anoint Hazael to be king over Syria:
And Jehu the son of Nimshi shalt thou anoint to be king over Israel: and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel–meholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room.
And it shall come to pass, that him that escapeth the sword of Hazael shall Jehu slay: and him that escapeth from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha slay.
And Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben–hadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.
And the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and go, meet the man of God, and enquire of the Lord by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?

So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Ben–hadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the Lord hath shewed me that he shall surely die.
And he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept.

And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.
And Hazael said, But what, is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha answered, The Lord hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.
So he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, He told me that thou shouldest surely recover.
And it came to pass on the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
But Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart: for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, which made Israel to sin.
In those days the Lord began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel;
From Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
Then Hazael king of Syria went up, and fought against Gath, and took it: and Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem.

And Jehoash king of Judah took all the hallowed things that Jehoshaphat, and Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own hallowed things, and all the gold that was found in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and in the king’s house, and sent it to Hazael king of Syria: and he went away from Jerusalem.
And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Ben–hadad the son of Hazael, all their days.
But Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

And the Lord was gracious unto them, and had compassion on them, and had respect unto them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, neither cast he them from his presence as yet.

Yea, all Israel have transgressed thy law, even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.

And he hath confirmed his words, which he spake against us, and against our judges that judged us, by bringing upon us a great evil: for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.
So Hazael king of Syria died; and Ben–hadad his son reigned in his stead.

And Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took again out of the hand of Ben–hadad the son of Hazael the cities, which he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Three times did Joash beat him, and recovered the cities of Israel.

Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And the king of Assyria hearkened unto him: for the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, and took it, and carried the people of it captive to Kir, and slew Rezin.
